newsitem.title: INDIA: Hindu party fails to win key north Indian state.
newsitem.headline: Hindu party fails to win key north Indian state.

text.p: Hindu nationalists failed to win an outright majority in elections in India's most populous state on Friday but retained enough clout to challenge Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.

With results for all but one of the 425 seats in the Uttar Pradesh legislature declared, the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) had won 177 seats, well short of the outright majority the party had sought. Deve Gowda's United Front coalition was second with 134.
The BJP, which built its national foundations on a Hindu revivalist agenda in Uttar Pradesh in the late 1980s, had hoped to win control of the country's biggest electoral prize.
The north Indian state wields enormous influence in the federal parliament where it has the largest number of seats.
An alliance between the Congress party and its low-caste partner, the Hindu Bahujan Samaj Party or BSP, took 100 seats.
The polls had significance for Deve Gowda's stability in New Delhi because his centre-left coalition there depends on the Congress to survive against a BJP challenge in parliament.
Congress has insisted that the United Front back its candidate for chief minister in Uttar Pradesh, BSP leader Mayawati.
But the United Front's main component in Uttar Pradesh, the Samajwadi Party, wants its leader and Deve Gowda's defence minister, Mulayam Singh Yadav, to lead the state.
